General information.Name: Environmental impact of Oaxaca cheese production and wastewater from artisanal dairies under two scenarios in Aculco, State of Mexico
General information.Description: The environmental impacts in the artisan cheese sector in the central region of Mexico provide a particular panorama of the environmental situation of this industry. The objective of this study was to evaluate environmental impacts through a life cycle analysis in 10 impact categories: global warming, stratospheric ozone depletion, fine particle formation, ozone formation, terrestrial ecosystems, terrestrial acidification, eutrophication of fresh water, terrestrial ecotoxicity, human ecotoxicity. non-carcinogenic toxicity, scarcity of fossil resources and water consumption. And the calculation of the carbon footprint with the IPCC, 2013 of 1 kg of Oaxaca cheese in four dairies artisanal in the State of Mexico. The main hotspots were whey, transportation, and electricity. The reduction of the impact generated by wastewater can be associated with the implementation and improvement of eco-innovations such as the use of biodigesters, however their use generates impacts on SOD, TA, FA, TEc and FRs due to the composition of the whey residue. The renewal of refrigeration equipment is another alternative to reduce electricity consumption, which on average consumes 0.04 kWh per one kg of Oaxaca cheese in cheese factories that have new refrigerators, and 0.14 kWh when refrigerators are reused, mainly impacting the FRs. The average carbon footprint of Oaxaca cheese was 15.6 CO 2 kg eq, which allows us to have a measure of the behavior of this food. A sensitivity analysis was carried out with different scenarios with wastewater where it was found that the handling of whey is essential for reducing impacts.
General information.Tags: Artisanal cheese, WWT anaerobic, carbon footprint, Whey, Eco-innovations
General information.Technology Description: The LCA was carried out in accordance with ISO 14040 and ISO 14042. The software SimaPro® v.8.5.0.0 (PRé Sustainability, Amersfoort, Netherlands) was used to calculate the environmental impacts. Data was sourced from the Ecoinvent v.3 database, a Mexican database (MX) for electrical energy, and generic data from Rest of the World (RoW) and Global (GLO) datasets. The impact evaluation was made using the ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint impacts categories method, Herarquista (H) v 1.01. The carbon footprint was calculated with the IPCC 2013 method.

processDocumentation.LCI method: The LCA was carried out in accordance with ISO 14040. It consisted of four phases: the establishment of the scope and objectives, the elaboration of the environmental inventories, and the generation and interpretation of the results.
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: The functional unit was 1 kg of Oaxaca cheese. The life cycle analysis was characterized from the reception of raw milk at the producer's door until the exit of the product for retail sale. Data on milk production was left out of the system, although the raw material (milk) was considered as an input. Whey was considered an avoided product because it is re-used as food by pig farms. It was considered that 10% of whey is lost and allocated to wastewater.
processDocumentation.Data source information: Primary data was collected during on-site visits and interviews. Secondary data for inputs such as raw milk, detergent ingredients, and wastewater were obtained from the Ecoinvent v.3 database (Ecoinvent, Zurich, Switzerland). A Mexican database (MX) for electrical energy (Santoyo-Castelazo et al., 2011) was used. The remaining inputs were populated from generic data available in other databases (RoW, GLO).
processDocumentation.Data completeness: The inventories were calculated for each of the four dairies using data specific to Oaxaca cheese production. Monthly production data were first calculated, then annual averages were estimated for the functional unit.
processDocumentation.Data selection: The impact of milk prior to arriving at the dairy was eliminated from the calculation in order to focus on the critical points within the cheese production industry.
processDocumentation.Data treatment: The data for the inventories were obtained through direct observation and eighteen interviews. Information was corroborated with a veterinary doctor. The data are reflective of a one-year production cycle: Monthly production data were first calculated. Then, the annual averages were estimated for a functional unit of 1 kg of cheese. The values presented are the average of the four dairies studied.
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Four dairies were selected for the LCA. The information required for the LCA was collected during on-site visits. Interviews were carried out with informants at the dairies and other social actors in the productive chain. Participants were identified using the snowball method.
processDocumentation.Use advice: The lack of databases specific to Mexico does not detract from the analysis, as the validity of using generic global data to approximate certain inputs for environmental impact assessment has been confirmed. The study presents an average of four different artisanal dairies, which have variations in electricity and water consumption.
processDocumentation.Completeness: The study provides a gate-to-gate inventory for the cheese production process, excluding the upstream impacts of raw milk production.

processDocumentation.Intended application: To evaluate environmental impacts of artisanal cheese production to identify hotspots and generate proposals for mitigating the environmental impact, contributing toward the competitiveness (ecofriendly, eco-labelling, circular economy) of the small-scale cheese industry.
